To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

finite size corrections to the BEC critical temperature of a relativistic gas of massless particles confined in a rectangular cavity have been calculated using the heat kernel method and that in the presence of strong spatial anisotropy the condensation occurs in multisteps.
we have calculated finite number and finite size corrections to the relativistic critical temperature of a Bose-Einstein condensate.

(1) finite size corrections to critical temperature in a rectangular cavity are obtained by the use of heat kernel method; (2) the critical temperature in lower dimensional systems can be calculated by zeta-function regularization; (3) the critical temperature can be calculated for the case when the system is anisotropic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the finite size effects in a relativistic ideal boson gas confined to a rectangular cavity.
the finite number and finite size effect in the Bose-Einstein condensations of a relativistic boson gas confined in a rectangular cavity.
the effects of finite size and finite number of particles on the Bose-Einstein condensate of a relativistic gas in a rectangular box.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the finite number and finite size corrections are not negligible in the relativistic Bose-Einsstein condensation.
the finite number and finite size effect on the critical temperature is not a simple additive correction, but is an intricate interplay between the two.
the critical temperature of relativistic Bose-Einsteins condensate in a finite rectangular box is lower than the critical temperature in infinite volume.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the finite size corrections are important for a relativistic ideal bosonic gas in the low temperature limit.
, finite size corrections to critical temperatures of relativistic Bose-Einsenstein condensation are calculated.
the condensation in the presence of strong magnetic field is not possible in the three dimensional system, but it can occur in lower dimensional systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
finite size effects are more important in the presence of anisotropy.
the critical temperatures of the lower dimensional systems can be tuned by the anisotropic parameter.
the finite size effects in the relativistic BEC are much more pronounced than those in the non-relativistic BEC.
